spots.name: Hassan II Mosque
spots.summary: The Hassan II Mosque is a mosque in Casablanca, Morocco. It is the second largest mosque in Africa and one of the largest mosques in the world. Its minaret is the world's second tallest minaret at 210 metres (689 ft).

spots.name: Casablanca Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Casablanca Cathedral, or Church of the Sacred Heart, is a former church located west of the Arab League Park in Casablanca, Morocco.

spots.name: Mohammed V Square
spots.summary: Mohammed V Square is a public square of historical and symbolic significance located in central Casablanca, Morocco. It was established in 1916 at the beginning of the French protectorate in Morocco under Resident-general Hubert Lyautey, on a design by architects Henri Prost and Joseph Marrast.

spots.name: United Nations Square
spots.summary: United Nations Square is a public square in the center of Casablanca, Morocco. It has been central in the history of Casablanca.

spots.name: Casablanca Twin Center
spots.summary: The Casablanca Twin Center is a complex of two skyscrapers located at Casablanca, Morocco. The two structures, the West Tower and the East Tower, have 28 floors each.

spots.name: Casablanca Clock Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Casablanca Clock Tower is a clock tower in Casablanca, Morocco. Located in United Nations Square, the tower is a 1993 reproduction of one of the oldest French-built structures in the city.

spots.name: Ettedgui Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ettedgui Synagogue is a synagogue in the medina of Casablanca, Morocco. It was rededicated by King Mohammed VI of Morocco on December 20, 2016, after it was restored. A government grant of about $844,000 funded the restorations, according to the Maghreb Arab Press.

spots.name: Arab League Park
spots.summary: The Arab League Park is an urban park in Casablanca, Morocco. It is located in the center of the city, west of Hassan II Boulevard, east of Roudani Boulevard and Algiers Street, and south east of the Church of the Sacred Heart. The park covers 30 acres of land, and is bisected by Moulay Youssef Boulevard.

spots.name: Equestrian statue of Hubert Lyautey
spots.summary: The equestrian statue of Hubert Lyautey is a public sculpture that commemorates Hubert Lyautey, the first resident-general of the French protectorate in Morocco, in Casablanca, Morocco.

spots.name: Temple Beth-El

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Temple Beth-El also called Beit-El or the Algerian Temple, is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue in the Sidi Belyout district of Casablanca, Morocco.

spots.name: Casablanca Finance City Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Casablanca Finance City Tower also known as the CFC Tower is a 28–story office building in Casablanca, Morocco. Built between 2016 and 2019, the tower stands at 136 m (446 ft) tall and is the fourth tallest building in Morocco.

spots.name: Al-Mohammadi Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Al-Mohammadi Mosque is a large mosque in the Habous quarter of Casablanca, Morocco. It was built circa 1935 and its construction was sponsored by Sultan Mohammed V, after whom it is named.

spots.name: Notre-Dame de Lourdes Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Notre-Dame de Lourdes Church is a Roman Catholic church in modernist style in Casablanca, Morocco. It was built in 1954 by architect Achille Dangleterre and engineer Gaston Zimmer.

spots.name: Stade Mohammed V
spots.summary: Stade Mohammed V is a multi-purpose stadium is situated in the western part of the Maârif neighborhood of central Casablanca, Morocco. The stadium has a seating capacity of 45,000 and it is the oldest football stadium in Morocco.

spots.name: Museum of Moroccan Judaism

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: The Museum of Moroccan Judaism is a museum of Jewish life in Morocco in Casablanca, Morocco.

spots.name: Assunna Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Assunna Mosque is a mosque designed by Jean-François Zevaco in a modernist architectural style in Casablanca, Morocco in 1966. It features brutalist architectural elements such as raw concrete. It is located at the junction of Blvd. 2 Mars and Blvd. Modibo Keïta.

spots.name: Ould el-Hamra Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ould el-Hamra Mosque is a mosque in the medina of Casablanca first erected in 1789. Along with the Ettedgui Synagogue and the Church of San Buenaventura, it is of the three buildings representing the three Abrahamic religions in a space of 250 m2 in the medina.

spots.name: Al-Quds Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Al-Quds Mosque, formerly Église de Sainte Marguerite, is a mosque in the Roches Noires neighborhood of Casablanca, Morocco. It was originally built as a church built in a Neo-Gothic style, but it was converted into a mosque after Morocco's independence.

spots.name: Church of San Buenaventura

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of San Buenaventura is a former Roman Catholic church, located in the Medina of Casablanca, Morocco. The church was founded by Franciscans in c. 1890. Built on territory Sultan Hassan I of Morocco granted to King Alfonso XII, it was the seat of the Spanish church in Casablanca from the late 19th century.

spots.name: Abderrahman Slaoui Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Abderrahman Slaoui Museum is a museum in Casablanca, Morocco. It is named after Abderrahman Slaoui, Moroccan businessman and art collector who died in 2001. The museum was founded by the Abderrahman Slaoui Foundation, and has been open since May 2012.

spots.name: Larbi Zaouli Stadium
spots.summary: Larbi Zaouli Stadium is a multi-use stadium in Casablanca, Morocco. It is used mostly for TAS Casablanca & SC Casablanca (Women).

spots.name: Larbi Benbarek Stadium
spots.summary: The Larbi Benbarek Stadium, originally known as Philip Stadium, is a multi-purpose stadium in Casablanca, Morocco. It is mostly used mostly for football matches and it hosted the home matches of Casablanca's clubs until the Stade Mohamed V opened. The stadium has a capacity of 20,000 spectators.
